QuestionText: MS Paint is used mainly to —
Options: A) Draw and edit pictures on a computer
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: MS Paint is a simple graphics/drawing application included with Windows.

QuestionText: Which tool in MS Paint draws a straight line?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Line tool draws a straight line between two points when you click and drag.

QuestionText: The Eraser tool in MS Paint is used to —
Options: A) Remove or erase parts of a drawing
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Eraser removes pixels from the drawing, replacing them with the background colour.

QuestionText: Which tool fills a closed area with colour in MS Paint?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Fill/Paint Bucket tool floods a selected area with the chosen foreground colour.

QuestionText: To UNDO the last action in MS Paint, press —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Ctrl + Z is the universal keyboard shortcut to undo the last action in most applications.

QuestionText: The 'Select' tool in MS Paint allows you to —
Options: A) Select a rectangular area to move, copy, or delete
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The rectangular selection tool draws a selection box around an area so it can be moved or modified.

QuestionText: To SAVE a file in MS Paint, press —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Ctrl + S saves the current file in its existing format and location.

QuestionText: Which MS Paint tool allows you to pick a colour already in your picture?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Colour Picker/Eyedropper samples the exact colour at the cursor position and sets it as the active colour.

QuestionText: What file format is the default save format in older versions of MS Paint?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Older MS Paint versions default to the BMP (Bitmap) format, which stores each pixel individually.

QuestionText: To draw a perfect circle in MS Paint, hold ___ while using the Oval tool.
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Holding Shift while drawing with the Oval/Ellipse tool constrains it to a perfect circle.

QuestionText: MS Word is a —
Options: A) Word processing application for creating documents
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: MS Word is Microsoft's word processing software for creating, formatting, and editing text documents.

QuestionText: Which tab in MS Word contains the 'Bold', 'Italic', and 'Underline' buttons?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Home tab contains basic text formatting options including Bold (Ctrl+B), Italic (Ctrl+I), and Underline (Ctrl+U).

QuestionText: To make text BOLD in MS Word, press —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Ctrl + B toggles bold formatting on selected text.

QuestionText: What does the cursor blinking in a MS Word document indicate?
Options: A) The insertion point — where text will be typed
D) The end of the document
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The blinking cursor (insertion point) shows exactly where the next typed character will appear.

QuestionText: To select ALL text in an MS Word document, press —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Ctrl + A selects all content in the current document.

QuestionText: Which MS Word feature checks for spelling errors?
Options: A) Spell Check (Review tab → Spelling & Grammar)
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Spelling & Grammar checker identifies misspellings and grammatical errors, suggesting corrections.

QuestionText: What does 'font size' control in MS Word?
Options: A) How large or small the text appears
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Font size is measured in points (pt); larger numbers = bigger text. Common sizes: 12pt (body), 24pt+ (headings).

QuestionText: The 'Paragraph alignment' buttons in MS Word include Left, Centre, Right, and —
Options: A) Justify (spreads text evenly across the line width)
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Justified alignment stretches spaces between words so both left and right margins are perfectly straight.

QuestionText: The Zoom tool in MS Paint magnifies the view to —
Options: A) Make part of the drawing appear larger for detailed editing
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Zooming in allows precise pixel-level editing of small details in a drawing.

QuestionText: A 'header' in MS Word appears —
Options: A) At the top of every page (for page title/number)
B) Only on the first page
C) In the middle of the page
D) At the bottom of every page
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Headers and footers are areas outside the main body that repeat on specified pages, used for page numbers, titles, etc.

QuestionText: 'Track Changes' in MS Word is useful for —
Options: A) Showing edits made to a document so reviewers can accept or reject them
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Track Changes marks additions, deletions, and formatting changes so collaborators can review them.

QuestionText: The 'Clipboard' in MS Word temporarily stores —
Options: A) Copied or cut text/objects until pasted
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Clipboard holds recently cut or copied content for pasting, and can hold multiple items.

QuestionText: What is the shortcut to open 'Find and Replace' in MS Word?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace, which locates specific text and replaces it with new text throughout the document.

QuestionText: What is the difference between 'Save' and 'Save As' in MS Word?
Options: A) Save overwrites the current file; Save As lets you choose a new name or location
C) Save As is for images only
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: 'Save' (Ctrl+S) updates the existing file; 'Save As' (F12) lets you create a new copy with a different name/format/location.

QuestionText: To insert an image into an MS Word document, go to —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: The Insert tab contains options for adding pictures, shapes, tables, charts, and other objects.

QuestionText: Hanging indent in MS Word means —
Options: A) The first line is flush left and all following lines are indented
C) Only the first line is indented
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Hanging indents are used in bibliographies/references: the first line starts at the margin; subsequent lines are indented.

QuestionText: Which MS Word feature allows you to see how the document will look when printed?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Print Preview shows the exact layout with margins, headers, and footers as it will appear on paper.

QuestionText: In MS Paint, the 'Pencil' and 'Brush' tools differ because —
Options: A) Pencil draws thin precise 1-pixel lines; Brush draws with variable width and softness
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Pencil is a hard-edged single-pixel tool; Brush offers different sizes and textures for artistic strokes.

QuestionText: 'AutoCorrect' in MS Word automatically —
Options: A) Fixes common typing mistakes as you type (e.g., 'teh' → 'the')
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: AutoCorrect corrects common typos and capitalization errors in real time as you type.

QuestionText: A Table of Contents in MS Word is most efficiently created using —
Options: A) Heading styles applied to headings, then References → Table of Contents
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: MS Word automatically generates a Table of Contents from paragraphs formatted with Heading 1/2/3 styles.

QuestionText: In MS Word, 'Styles' are useful because —
Options: A) They apply consistent formatting across the document, making it easy to update all headings at once
C) They are just for headings
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Styles link format settings to text; changing a style automatically updates all text using that style throughout.

QuestionText: PNG and JPEG are both image file formats. PNG is preferred when —
Options: A) Transparency is needed or the image has sharp edges and text (lossless)
B) A very small file size is needed
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: PNG uses lossless compression and supports transparency; JPEG uses lossy compression, losing quality but smaller file size.

QuestionText: A bitmap (raster) image becomes blurry when enlarged because —
Options: A) It is made of fixed pixels that spread out when the image is scaled up
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Raster images have a fixed resolution; enlarging them beyond original size interpolates pixels, causing blurring.

QuestionText: Vector images (SVG) do NOT blur when resized because —
Options: A) They are defined by mathematical equations (paths), not pixels
B) They are stored in RAM
D) They are always in black and white
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Vector graphics are resolution-independent mathematical descriptions; they can scale to any size without quality loss.

QuestionText: The DPI (Dots Per Inch) setting for a printed image should be at least ___ for good print quality.
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Print quality requires ~300 DPI; 72 DPI is screen resolution. Below 300 DPI, printed images look pixelated.

QuestionText: MS Word's 'Mail Merge' feature is used to —
Options: A) Create personalised letters/emails for many recipients using a data source
B) Merge two documents into one
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Mail Merge combines a template document with a data source (e.g., contacts list) to produce personalised documents in bulk.

QuestionText: What does 'kerning' control in typography/word processing?
Options: A) The spacing between individual pairs of characters
B) The size of the font
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Kerning adjusts spacing between specific letter pairs (e.g., 'AV') to improve visual consistency and readability.

QuestionText: Which feature in MS Word allows you to see two versions of a document side by side for comparison?
Options: A) View → Compare Documents (or View → Side by Side)
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Word's Compare feature highlights differences between two document versions, or View Side by Side shows both simultaneously.

QuestionText: The colour model used by computer screens (RGB) mixes which three light colours?
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Screens use additive RGB colour mixing: Red+Green+Blue light at full intensity makes white; all off makes black.

QuestionText: CMYK colour model (used in printing) stands for —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: CMYK is a subtractive model used in colour printing: inks absorb light. K (Key) = Black, used for sharp text.

QuestionText: In MS Word, 'Section Breaks' are used to —
Options: A) Divide the document into sections with different formatting (e.g., landscape page in a portrait document)
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Section breaks allow different headers/footers, page orientation, or column layout within one document.

QuestionText: What is the difference between a raster image edited in MS Paint and a vector image edited in Inkscape?
Options: A) Paint edits individual pixels; Inkscape edits mathematical shapes that scale without quality loss
C) Inkscape can only draw lines
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Raster (pixel) editing in Paint suits photos; vector editing in Inkscape suits logos/icons that need to scale.

QuestionText: MS Word's 'Macros' allow users to —
Options: A) Record and replay a sequence of commands to automate repetitive tasks
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Macros record keystrokes and menu actions; running the macro replays them automatically, saving time on repetitive work.

QuestionText: The 'Widow and Orphan Control' setting in MS Word prevents —
Options: A) Single lines of a paragraph appearing alone at the top or bottom of a page
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Widow: a paragraph's last line alone at the top of a page. Orphan: first line alone at the bottom. This feature avoids both.

QuestionText: In which colour model would a designer choose colours when creating graphics for a website?
Options: A) RGB (Red Green Blue) — used for screen display
C) HSL — used for paint mixing
D) Pantone — used for industrial printing
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Web graphics are displayed on screens using RGB; CMYK is for print. Designers must use the right model for each medium.

QuestionText: What is 'anti-aliasing' in digital graphics?
Options: A) Smoothing jagged edges of shapes by blending colours at the edges to reduce the staircase effect
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Anti-aliasing blends edge pixels with surrounding colours, making curved/diagonal edges appear smooth on low-resolution screens.

QuestionText: A macro-enabled MS Word document has the extension —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: .docm is the macro-enabled Word format; .docx is standard (no macros). The 'm' stands for macro-enabled.

QuestionText: Using 'Styles' in MS Word instead of manual formatting makes documents —
Options: A) Easier to update consistently and improves accessibility for screen readers
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Semantic styles (Heading 1, Body Text) allow one-click reformatting and enable screen readers to understand document structure.

QuestionText: In MS Paint (3D or newer), the 'Magic Select' tool uses AI to —
Options: A) Automatically detect and cut out objects from their background
C) Change all colours at once
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: Magic Select uses AI object recognition to detect the edges of a subject, enabling background removal with one click.

QuestionText: A PNG file of 3840×2160 pixels at 8 bits per channel (RGB, 3 channels) would have an uncompressed size of approximately —
Topic: MS Paint and Introduction to MS Word
Explanation: 3840×2160×3 channels×1 byte = 24,883,200 bytes ≈ 23.7 MB uncompressed. PNG compresses this further.
